These augmented outliers are then blurred to further reduce their complexity. The authors evaluate their approach on a variety of image and text datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in OOD detection accuracy compared to baseline methods. The results suggest that the proposed method achieves performance comparable to models trained with real outliers, highlighting its practical utility. The paper also explores the relationship between the complexity of an input sample and its latent representation in the normalizing flow model, arguing that lower complexity inputs tend to concentrate in high-density regions of the latent space, leading to higher likelihoods. By introducing synthetic outliers, the authors aim to correct this bias and improve the model's ability to differentiate between in-domain and OOD data. The paper's main contribution lies in the specific combination of synthetic outlier generation and the softplus-based training objective, which is shown to be effective in mitigating the bias of normalizing flows towards low-complexity OOD samples.
